football_evidence.assessment: Most of the 2.0-point difference traces to home field (engine constant) (about 1.1 points), which the closing market has historically priced differently. That explains the gap; it does not make either number a bet.

In his last two games (Minnesota and Penn State), Underwood averaged 4.5 yards per attempt, against 8.3 in his four games before that.
Tommy Carr has completed 27 of 41 passes (65.9%) for 237 yards, 5.8 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and 1 interception in three games for Michigan, and has been sacked on 5 of 46 dropbacks.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Rutgers’ offensive line No. 19 nationally and Michigan’s No. 83.
contradicting: When Rutgers has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Rutgers’ offense has allowed a sack on 7.9% of its dropbacks, and Michigan’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Rutgers has the ball (big plays on the ground): Rutgers’ offense turns 7.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and Michigan’s defense gives up explosive gains on 1.6% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Michigan has the ball (big plays on the ground): Michigan’s offense turns 5.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Rutgers’ defense gives up explosive gains on 11.6% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
When Rutgers has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Rutgers’ offense averages 5.4 yards per carry, and Michigan’s defense allows 3.5 yards per carry (FBS average 5.0).
